chunks: From him, from al-‘Alā’, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked him about Salat al-Jumu‘ah during travel, and he said: You do as you do in Zuhr, and the Imam does not recite aloud in it. He only recites aloud when there is a sermon.
So the proper way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as applying to a state of taqiyyah and fear; that indicates this.

key_terms.التَّقِيَّةِ: dissimulation for protection, cited as the context for interpreting the reports
key_terms.السَّفَرِ: travel, the circumstance affecting the prayer ruling
key_terms.الظُّهْرِ: Zuhr prayer, used here as the model for how to perform it
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the prayer leader whose recitation ruling is described
key_terms.الْخَوْفِ: fear, paired with taqiyyah as the interpretive circumstance
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: the recitation in prayer, specifically whether it is audible
key_terms.خُطْبَةٌ: the sermon, whose presence changes the ruling of audible recitation
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the Friday prayer discussed in the ruling

ai.seo_question: How is Salat al-Jumu‘ah performed during travel according to this hadith in al-Istibsar?
ai.summary: This report addresses the ruling of Salat al-Jumu‘ah while traveling, stating that it is performed like Zuhr and without audible recitation by the Imam unless there is a sermon. The closing note explains that these reports are to be understood in the context of taqiyyah and fear, indicating a jurisprudential reconciliation of narrations.
